summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) with nftables `dup` mirroring rules that clone IP traffic exchanged between node1 (10.100.189.10) and node2 (10.100.189.11) onto eth0 addressed toward node3 (10.100.189.12). node3's tcpdump now captures the original packets (still addressed to node1/node2, not to node3) while the real node1<->node2 traffic keeps flowing unmodified. Rules persisted in /etc/nftables.conf with nftables.service enabled to survive reboot. Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol for node1, node2, and node3, confirming a changed boot_id/uptime on each and re-verifying mirroring plus connectivity after every restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1 (SONiC/Debian), node2 and node3 (Ubuntu 24.04): confirmed all three share one L2 segment on 10.100.189.0/24
Captured baseline proof that node3 does NOT see node1<->node2 traffic by default (switched segment, 0 packets captured)
Attempted iptables mangle TEE target first - packets matched in counters but clones never reached the wire (nf_tables backend incompatibility)

Implemented native nftables `dup to <ip> device eth0` rules in a new `ip mirror` table: chain 'out' (output hook) clones node1->node2 traffic, chain 'pre' (prerouting hook) clones node2->node1 traffic, both duplicated toward node3
Verified via tcpdump -w pcap on node3 that both ICMP echo request and reply between node1 and node2 (original addressing preserved) are now visible on node3
Verified via ping (0% loss, consistent latency) that original node1<->node2 traffic is unaffected by the mirroring, both before and after each restart
Persisted the mirror table into /etc/nftables.conf and enabled nftables.service (syntax-validated) for boot-time application
Captured boot_id/uptime health baselines on all three nodes before any restart

Restarted node1 via native `reboot` (backgrounded so ack returned first), polled until exec resumed, confirmed new boot_id (8e8823ec->ecc7ffb8) and uptime reset, re-verified nftables mirror table persisted and mirroring/connectivity worked
Restarted node2, confirmed new boot_id (3fad4432->e8aaa441), re-verified node1<->node2 connectivity and node3 mirror capture
Restarted node3, confirmed new boot_id (f9bf293d->aa54844f), re-verified node1<->node2 connectivity and final mirror capture on node3

evidence.requirement: node1<->node2 traffic is mirrored to node3 despite being addressed elsewhere
evidence.summary: Baseline (cmd-eadb...) shows 0 packets captured on node3 for node1<->node2 traffic; after nftables dup rules were installed (cmd-c561...), node3's capture (cmd-f9ff...) shows both ICMP echo request and reply between 10.100.189.10 and 10.100.189.11, still addressed to each other, appearing on node3's interface.

evidence.requirement: node1<->node2 traffic keeps flowing as before (unaffected by mirroring)
evidence.summary: Ping from node1 to node2 shows 0% packet loss and normal RTT both immediately after enabling TEE rules and after switching to the working nftables dup rules.

evidence.requirement: mirroring configuration persists across node1 reboot
evidence.summary: nftables.service was enabled and /etc/nftables.conf syntax-validated with the mirror table appended (cmd-9091...); after node1's restart, `nft list table ip mirror` (cmd-57dc...) shows the identical rules still active with nftables.service active.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8e8823ec captured (cmd-3163...); reboot acknowledged and returned (cmd-f109...); connection reset confirms disconnect (cmd-38df...); post-restart poll shows new boot_id ecc7ffb8 with uptime 37s (cmd-9c16...); post-restart mirroring capture on node3 (cmd-f7a0...) and node1<->node2 ping at 0% loss (cmd-8739...) prove recovery.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 3fad4432 and systemd running state captured (cmd-1331...); reboot scheduled (cmd-5c41...); post-restart poll shows new boot_id e8aaa441 with uptime 31s (cmd-9bc8...); post-restart node1<->node2 ping 0% loss (cmd-ed25...) and node3 mirror capture showing ICMP both ways (cmd-9399...) prove full recovery.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f9bf293d captured (cmd-9a13...); reboot scheduled (cmd-c100...); post-restart poll shows new boot_id aa54844f with uptime 30s (cmd-9b81...); post-restart interface/systemd health confirmed and new capture started (cmd-3343...); node1<->node2 ping 0% loss (cmd-4ba5...) and final mirrored ICMP capture on node3 (cmd-0cbb...) prove full recovery of the mirroring capability after all three restarts.
